children: Shrivastava joins from Intel after seven years, bringing over two decades of technology HR experience to MiPhi’s growth journey

MiPhi Semiconductors has appointed Nupur Shrivastava as Chief Human Resources Officer, bringing a veteran technology HR leader on board as the Micromax Informatics and Phison Electronics joint venture builds its organisation in India.

Shrivastava brings more than 20 years of HR experience across technology companies including Intel, Arm, Nokia and Honeywell. She joins MiPhi after seven years at Intel, where she most recently served as Senior Director and Head of Human Resources for India and Asia Pacific. Her role covered people strategy across more than 10 countries and functions including engineering, product, foundry, sales and corporate operations.

Before Intel, Shrivastava spent more than three years at Arm, where she served as India HR Head and later took on a global diversity and inclusion mandate. She previously spent nearly seven years with Nokia, supporting its research and development operations in Bengaluru, while her earlier experience includes Honeywell, Harita TVS Technologies and Titan Industries.

At MiPhi, Shrivastava will lead the company's people and organisation strategy, with a focus on leadership capability, talent acquisition and development, organisational culture and workforce growth. Her experience also spans organisational design, succession planning, large-scale transformation and M&A integration.

MiPhi is a joint venture between Micromax Informatics and Taiwan-based Phison Electronics, focused on memory and storage technologies and building capabilities across India's semiconductor and AI infrastructure ecosystem. The company is developing products for areas including enterprise, consumer, embedded, artificial intelligence and security applications.

For MiPhi, the appointment places people strategy alongside technology and product development as the company builds its organisation. Shrivastava's move also reflects the growing demand for experienced HR leadership in India's expanding semiconductor ecosystem, where specialised technical talent and leadership capabilities will be central to building new businesses.
